claims.statement: Configuration is read directly from process.env at module load by each consumer with hard-coded in-code fallbacks — there is no config loader, schema, or startup validation — so a missing variable never blocks boot and instead silently redirects a service to a default endpoint or credential.

The web app reads only three application variables: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL as the API base for every fetch (fallback http://localhost:4000/api), and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY for the Supabase browser client (fallbacks https://placeholder.supabase.co and placeholder-anon-key).

NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY are documented in neither .env.example nor any compose file, so shipped configurations run against the placeholder Supabase host; this degrades rather than fails because getAuthToken() catches client/session errors and returns null, and apiFetch then omits the Authorization header, leaving the app in guest/local-persistence mode.

NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is a build-time constant: Dockerfile.web sets ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:4000/api in the builder stage right before the web build, so the published image's client bundle always contains that value and setting NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL on the web service in compose changes only the runtime environment of next start, not the inlined URL.

JWT_SECRET has three non-equivalent resolution paths — docker-compose.prod.yml injects ${JWT_SECRET:-please-change-me}, docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.dev.yml set no JWT_SECRET at all so the module-load fallback 'dev-secret-change-in-production' in auth.ts applies, and a hand-run process uses whatever .env supplies — so which secret a container verifies against depends on how it was started, and because both fallbacks are public an API without an explicit override accepts tokens anyone can mint. The value is captured once at module load, so changing it requires a process restart.

The Prisma datasource declares both url=env("DATABASE_URL") and directUrl=env("DIRECT_URL"), and the API image entrypoint exports DIRECT_URL="${DIRECT_URL:-$DATABASE_URL}" before running prisma migrate deploy when DATABASE_URL is set (skipping migrations and logging catalog-only mode when it is not). The source-build and dev compositions set both variables to the same DSN, but docker-compose.prod.yml gives DIRECT_URL only to sync-worker, so in the pull-based stack the entrypoint default — not compose — is what satisfies the API's directUrl.

storage-service.ts resolves every storage setting as S3_ENDPOINT??AWS_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION??AWS_REGION??'auto', S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID??AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID??'', S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY??AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY??'', S3_BUCKET??S3_BUCKET_NAME??'forceorg-media', CDN_BASE_URL??PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL??'' — S3_* winning — because .env.example documents S3_* names while all compose files inject AWS_*/S3_BUCKET_NAME/PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL.

Because storage aliasing happens before the S3Client is constructed, forcePathStyle: Boolean(S3_ENDPOINT) is driven by the already-resolved endpoint (either name), enabling path-style addressing for MinIO/SeaweedFS and disabling it on the https://s3.amazonaws.com fallback; the empty-string credential fallback is passed straight into the client's credentials so the SDK ambient credential chain is never consulted, meaning prod compose's empty AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY defaults surface as upload-route errors rather than a startup failure.

uploadImage derives the persisted public URL by precedence — CDN_BASE_URL/PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL (trailing slashes stripped) + key, else resolved endpoint + /BUCKET/key, else https://BUCKET.s3.amazonaws.com/key — so an unset CDN base in production compose mints container-internal http://s3:9000 URLs, and objects are written with CacheControl public, max-age=31536000, immutable.

S3_BUCKET takes precedence over S3_BUCKET_NAME, so a partially exported .env using the documented bucket forceorg-media can point uploads at a bucket the local SeaweedFS store never provisions, since compose creates and expects forceorg-miniatures.
The API's non-storage defaults are PORT=4000 and a single CORS_ORIGIN of http://localhost:3000 applied with credentials: true; Dockerfile.api additionally bakes ENV PORT=4000 into the image.

The sync worker requires DATABASE_URL for its Prisma writes and treats ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL as best-effort: sendAlert() returns immediately when unset, is only invoked when the pass reports updated or errored endpoints, and swallows webhook exceptions with console.error, so no-delta runs never alert and alerts are not durable.

docker-compose.dev.yml uses host-side interpolation WEB_PORT:-3000 and API_PORT:-4000 both for published ports and for CORS_ORIGIN and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, so WEB_PORT=13000 API_PORT=14000 ./scripts/dev.sh up keeps CORS and the browser API base consistent while the servers still bind 3000/4000 inside the containers.

.env.dev is a committed, safe-to-commit file attached to the shared x-dev-common anchor and currently carries only NODE_ENV=development; the toolchain one-shot joins only the image anchor so it does not read .env.dev but still receives NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL derived from API_PORT, which matters because e2e runs next build inside it.

Playwright config defaults use.baseURL to http://localhost:3456 unless PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_BASE_URL is set, pins the webServer to npx next start -p 3456 with NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL defaulting to http://localhost:4000/api and reuseExistingServer: false, and enables forbidOnly, 2 retries, and a single worker when CI is truthy.

docker-compose.prod.yml is parameterized almost entirely through host variables with public placeholder defaults — FORCEORG_TAG (latest), JWT_SECRET (please-change-me), CORS_ORIGIN, POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_PASSWORD/POSTGRES_DB interpolated into the Postgres service and the API/sync-worker DSNs, AWS_REGION, S3_BUCKET_NAME, PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL (empty), AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (empty), API_PORT/WEB_PORT, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL — while AWS_ENDPOINT is hard-coded to http://s3:9000 and therefore not redirectable, so an unset environment boots a fully working but publicly-credentialed stack pointed at the bundled SeaweedFS.

Both compose files interpolate ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL with an empty-string fallback so the host value passes through to the one-shot worker, while the scheduled GitHub Actions workflow supplies DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL, and ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL from repository secrets.

The dev compose api service injects the same AWS-native storage names as production (AWS_ENDPOINT http://s3:9000, AWS_REGION us-east-1, minioadmin credentials, S3_BUCKET_NAME forceorg-miniatures, PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL http://localhost:9000/forceorg-miniatures), and the dev toolchain sets PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/pw-browsers on a shared volume that the e2e command checks before running.

In docker-compose.prod.yml the sync-worker's DIRECT_URL interpolates its password from ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres} while the DATABASE_URL one line above uses ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgrespassword}, so with no host POSTGRES_PASSWORD set the two DSNs the same worker receives carry different credentials — latent today because Prisma uses directUrl only for migrate/introspection and the worker does not migrate.

The 'Default in compose' column of docs/DEPLOYMENT.md section 2 describes the source-build composition (PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL http://localhost:9000/forceorg-miniatures, minioadmin storage credentials), which differs materially from docker-compose.prod.yml where those same variables default to empty — so the same documentation page describes two different runtime shapes for storage.

In docker-compose.dev.yml the api service declares its own environment: block alongside <<: *dev-common, which replaces rather than merges the anchor mapping — the api container therefore receives the AWS-native storage names and dev DSNs but not the anchor's NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, and only the web and toolchain services get that interpolated value.
